title:

 – eMedals
description: Description The collection consists of a 1920 Austrian travel passport (99x143mm, better than very fine) and 46 photos and picture postcards (54x80mm to 129x178mm, very fine to near mint), dated between 1916 and 1931. The items are connected to the Kutnar family, with several family members appearing on the pictures. The passport is issued to Otto Kutnar from Korneuburg (Austria), born 1905, for the purpose of traveling to Yugoslavia. A card-mounted photo dated to February 24, 1909 and showing an Austro-Hungarian Master Sergeant is signed “Kutnar”, with the first name being illegible. A man in the same rank stands next to a woman on a picture dated to May 1916. A postcard showing a Sergeant of the Austro-Hungarian army with an extensive medal bar is to Lieutenant Hans Kutnar. Later pictures identify a similar looking man as “Papa Janez”, “Papa” meaning “daddy” and Janez being the Slovenian form of Hans. Janez is shown on a studio portrait from 1920 in a Yugoslavian uniform in the rank of Lieutenant in the Yugoslavian air force. He makes an appearance on several picture from the late 1920s, between 1927 and 1929, most of them taken at the Zagreb aerodrome. Many of these show planes, several show Janez’ children, Zvonko and Marjan, and his wife Miza. Two large photos show a gathering of Yugoslavian officers in 1930. Janez can be seen in the center of one, holding the rank of First Captain. The latest picture shows him standing in front of a plane in an army leather flight coat in 1931. A final picture, taken in Celje, Slovenia, shows a Yugoslavian air force soldier, in the rank of 2nd Lieutenant, possibly Janez’ son.

Based on German military organization of that era, this unit was part of the 31st Infantry Regiment (specifically the Infanterie-Regiment Graf Bose (1. Thüringisches) Nr. 31). During the war, the Ersatz (Replacement) Battalions played a crucial behind-the-scenes role. While the main regiment was fighting on the front lines—most notably at the Battle of Verdun and the Somme—the Ersatz units remained in the home garrisons (primarily in Altona and Plauen). Their primary mission was to process new recruits, provide basic training, and rehabilitate wounded soldiers until they were fit to be sent back to the active field regiments. Because these units were responsible for the "flow" of manpower, the Kompaniekommandant (Company Commander) held a position of significant paternal authority, overseeing the transition of young men from civilians to soldiers.
